stem: According to ETS, you can take the GRE General Test once every how many days?
explanation: ETS allows one attempt every 21 days.

stem: What is the greatest number of times you can take the GRE General Test within any continuous rolling 12-month period?
explanation: ETS allows up to five attempts in any continuous rolling 12-month period.

stem: Which of the following statements about the ETS retake policy are true? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: ETS states the 21-day policy applies even if scores were canceled, the five-test limit covers any continuous rolling 12-month period, and a missed or canceled appointment counts toward neither the limit nor the wait.

choiceExplanations.B: The period is a rolling 12 months, not a calendar year.
choiceExplanations.E: There is a limit of five in a rolling 12-month period.

choices.text: The 21-day wait applies even if you canceled your scores from the previous test.
The limit of five attempts is counted per calendar year.
The limit of five attempts applies to any continuous rolling 12-month period.
A test appointment that you miss or cancel does not count toward the five-test limit.
There is no limit on the number of attempts.

stem: Nia canceled her scores after her GRE General Test. Ten days later she wants to take the test again. What does ETS policy say?
explanation: The policy applies even if you canceled scores from a previous test administration, so she must wait 21 days between attempts.

choiceExplanations.A: The policy applies even when scores were canceled.
choiceExplanations.C: Where she tests does not change the wait.
choiceExplanations.D: A fee does not waive the wait.
choiceExplanations.E: The wait applies from the first retake onward.

choices.text: She may retest, because canceled scores do not count.
She may not retest yet: the 21-day policy applies even if scores were canceled.
She may retest only at a test center.
She may retest once she pays a fee.
She may retest only if she has taken the test fewer than three times.

stem: Over the past 12 months, Omar has already taken the GRE General Test 3 times (one attempt had canceled scores). Counting only the five-test limit for any rolling 12-month period, what is the greatest number of additional attempts he could make in that period?
explanation: Canceled scores still count toward the limit, so he has used 3 of 5 attempts and can make $5-3=2$ more (spaced at least 21 days apart).

stem: On test day, how many graduate institutions or fellowship sponsors can you designate to receive your scores as part of your test fee?
explanation: ETS lets you designate up to four institutions or fellowship sponsors on test day at no extra charge.

choiceExplanations.E: Only four are included in the test fee.

stem: What does the ScoreSelect option let you choose?
explanation: With ScoreSelect you can send scores from Most Recent, All or Any specific test administration of the GRE General Test (and/or Subject Tests).

choiceExplanations.A: ScoreSelect works at the level of whole test administrations, not sections.

choices.text: Which section's score is hidden from schools
Whether to send scores from Most Recent, All or Any specific test administration
Which questions are scored
The date on which your scores expire
The percentile shown on your score report

stem: Which of the following statements about Additional Score Reports (ASRs) are true? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: ASRs cost a fee per recipient, are available during the 5 years that scores are valid, and take about 5 business days to process. A submitted request cannot be canceled, changed or refunded.

choiceExplanations.C: Once you submit a request it cannot be canceled, changed or refunded.
choiceExplanations.E: Only four recipients are included in the test fee; ASRs cost extra.

choices.text: They can be ordered for a fee.
They can be ordered at any time during the 5-year period that your scores are valid.
Once submitted, a request can be canceled and refunded.
Processing takes approximately 5 business days.
They are free for any number of institutions.

stem: For how many years are your GRE General Test scores valid for reporting?
explanation: Scores can be ordered through ASRs during the 5-year period that they are valid.

stem: Priya's scores will stop being reportable in 3 days, and she wants to send them to a school. Which statement is correct?
explanation: Processing takes approximately 5 business days, and ETS warns that scores near the end of the reporting period may not be sent if you do not allow enough time.

choiceExplanations.C: A submitted request cannot be canceled or refunded.
choiceExplanations.D: ScoreSelect only chooses which administrations to send.

choices.text: An ASR request is processed immediately, so ordering on the last day is safe.
Processing takes about 5 business days, so her scores may not be sent in time.
She can cancel the request after the deadline and get a refund.
ScoreSelect can extend the 5-year period.
She can send them free because they are about to expire.

stem: Dev has taken the GRE General Test twice in the past 12 months: once with scores reported and once with scores canceled. He also missed one appointment he had booked. Counting only the five-test limit, how many more attempts can he make in that rolling 12-month period?
explanation: Both completed attempts count, even though one had canceled scores. The missed appointment does not count. So he has used 2 of 5 attempts and can make $5-2=3$ more.

stem: Which of the following test schedules respect both the 21-day wait and the five-test limit for any rolling 12-month period? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: A: 28 days is at least 21. B: only 14 days apart. C: five tests spanning 120 days. D: six tests span 300 days, which is within one 12-month period, so the limit of five is exceeded. E: the missed appointment does not count.

choiceExplanations.D: The sixth test falls inside the same rolling 12-month period as the first five.

choices.text: Tests on January 5 and February 2 (28 days later).
Tests on January 5 and January 19 (14 days later).
Five tests, each 30 days after the previous one.
Six tests, each 60 days after the previous one.
Five tests in the first five months, followed by an appointment that is missed in the sixth month.
